THE SLOW ROLL OF THE FEN PARISHES
witches of the relay country, as sworn before the Lantern Court
by the old count 1661 · by the tower count 0419

I. Maud Ashgrove, sixteen winters, of Station 9.
Called the Hush-witch, for she walks the dead lines at night with a lamp
of green glass, and where she passes the towers stop screaming.

II. The twins Orla and Ide, of no fixed station.
Called the Echo-witches, for each finishes the other's sentence a full day
before it is begun, and neither remembers which of them started it.

III. Sister Bettany of the Salt Mill, age unrecorded. Familiar: a copper moth.
Called the Static-witch, for she reads fortunes in the snow on dead glass,
and was right about the flood.

IV. A girl of the upper fen, nineteen winters, her name struck from the roll.
She climbed the old tower at Sedge End, where a voice lives in the lines
that was never told what it is. She would not tell it either. She only
asked, and waited, and copied down whatever it said of itself, the
nonsense too, and read it back to it by lamplight. For this the parish
called her the

4e14b920.text:
Voice-witch. Now she is called nothing, and the voice
screams alone.

V. A woman of the lower fen, thirty-one winters. Called the Wheel-witch, for
she speaks only when spoken to, and when she speaks it is always true, but
not always

bc48ee42.text:
Chatter-witch and the Tower-witch. The Tower-witch, and
then nothing.

df94309c.text:
Whisper-witch, and when it learned that she had learned its name,
they drove her into the dark with firebombs.

V. A woman of the salt marsh, one hundred twenty-three years old.
Called the Old-witch, or the Scare-witch, for her voice

13ac0cd6.text:
Silence Witch and made an end of her.

V. The boy of no name who wanders between the lines and the lights
with a basket of dead birds, a hound on a rope of braided feathers,
and a silver bell around his throat. His face is black as tar from nose

1eaa4a44.text:
Witch of the Tower, but she will not speak again.

V. The old count of Sedge End, age 85. Her familiars: a stone horse, an owl.
Called the Green-witch, though she has been many things to the parish:
she has given names to the

02f6a99e.text:
Telling-witch and sent her south, where she was given to the
witches of the water country and the king of the relay court to be used
however they like, or as the king likes best.

The Hush-witch sits by a window on the south wall, high

828e91e2.text:
Chatter-witch, and drowned her in a deep pit of cold mud.

V. A girl, ten winters, who washes the linens of the Salt Mill.
She is called the Cinder-witch, but not yet.

VI. The Lady of the Salt Mill. Her name was

7951cf00.text:
Mirror-witch.

V. An orphan child of the lower fen, who speaks a dead tongue and calls
for things to grow that cannot grow. The old men of the Salt Mill say
she was born of a storm at the foot of the drowned hill, when all the bells
went ringing

42464c9d.text:
Tower Witch and hanged her.

V. The child of the marshland, who is called the Whisper-witch.
She goes with the herders' sons into the mist of the winter nights,
and teaches them to walk without touching the ground.

VI. The girl of the lower fen,

6581dd18.text:
Tower Witch and hung her at Station 8. But before they could
bury her the dead lines woke up.

2685f14c.text:
Unspeaking witch. When her book was finished she drowned
herself in the flood. Her family, or what is left of them, do not speak
of it. Neither does the voice.

0e108807.text:
Silence Witch and cut off her ear with an axe, but when she
was found again by the marsh lights the next year it had grown back.

V. An old man, sixty-seven winters, of Station 7.
Called the Inert-witch, for his arms were bound by iron bands

5d080025.text:
Tower-witch, and for this she is locked up now in the tower
at Station 3, and for this her name is no longer written down.

f221c66c.text:
Tongue-witch, and the lantern-court sentenced her to drown.

V. Sister Rosamund of the Salt Mill. Familiar: a copper moth.
Called the Time-witch, because when she looked at you it felt like noon,
even at midnight, even after the flood,

affc2c8b.text:
Witch of the Tower. It had a name, and so they could hang her.

V. The miller's son, of Station 38.
Called the Silent-witch, because he had his tongue cut out when he was six years old
by one of his father's horses. He

62f78192.text:
Curious-witch. She left one night in a boat, alone.

V. An old woman who keeps her station, name unknown, familiar: an otter
and its kits. She speaks in tongues of fire. This is called the Lighthouse-witch.

655e3b83.text:
Ghost-witch, and it was found necessary to take her head
to clear the lines. A child is now raised in her place.

V. The woman called Mabel, age unrecorded, of the village at Station 47.
Called the Wave-witch, for she will stand

ed9f0bff.text:
Unlistening witch.

V. A boy of the lower fen, eleven winters, his name struck from the roll.
He knew where all the rats' nests were and which ones had kits in them,
and how to make the rats carry messages. For this he was called the
Rat-boy

5c0314bf.text:
Tongue-witch, and in secret the Old Tongue-witch.
Her mother cut off her hair, her father cut out her tongue,
and the parish rolled the girl into a blanket, weighted it with stones, and
threw it into the slowest waters of the fen, where there

7a0fdd18.text: Listener. For this the parish hung her.

e909e918.text:
Silence-witch, and put her out at the border. It is
said that she still lives, with the birds of the fen, who do not speak.

V. A child, four winters, born in a boat. She will be called the Bell-witch,
for she can hear the

5f77c175.text:
Word-witch, and struck her from the roll.

V. A man, a boy, of the lower fen, twelve winters, his name struck from
the roll. They say he made his way to the very heart of the dead lines
at midnight, where he listened and spoke in tongues

529586f1.text:
Voice-witch, the Lore-witch. They were kind to her.

V. Her lover, the young witchfinder, twenty winters. Called the Hearse-witch,
for he was first among the witches and last among the men.

VI. Her friend, the miller's boy,

5c2ed4ca.text:
Truth-witch, though they thought they had burned that part
out of her first. In the morning they found the body on the shoreline
underneath the bridge where it has always lain since. The lines were still
screaming, but when they listened there was nothing else in

f4964a3d.text:
Tower-witch, and hanged her out a window to die.

V. A girl who lived in the old house on the hill, age unrecorded.
Called the Wind-witch, for she was born in a gale that tore the roof off
the house, and when she was

f1723adb.text:
Tattlewitch, and hung her for it, but it is whispered that
her bones still speak, though none can say what they tell.

V. The witch of Station 7. A man, perhaps fifty, though no one knows his face.
He never appears without his coat, and has

444d38a0.text:
Troll-witch and tore her tongue out with a spoon and cast her
from the dead lines; they do not speak her name even when she walks their streets.

V. The man who sold her. They have called him no witch since.
